diagnoses.label: no build-fix skill for CI/tox failures
diagnoses.general_pattern: The provided skill bundle contains no guidance for diagnosing or repairing Python build/CI failures (tox environments, missing optional dependencies, flaky/time-based test assertions, pyproject.toml/tox.ini alignment). The four preloaded skills cover CI log analysis, Temporal testing, pytest style, and uv usage—none map to the presented task of restoring a green tox-based build across multiple Python versions.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Preloaded skills are analyze-ci, temporal-python-testing, testing-python, uv-package-manager. Task requires fixing a tox build for AgentOps-AI. Verifier shows tox py37/38/39 missing interpreters and test_record_timestamp failing due to millisecond-precision timestamp collision (init_timestamp == end_timestamp). Agent addressed only the ImportError, explicitly declared the timestamp failure 'out of scope,' and finished; verifier reports Build failed in the passed job.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A decision procedure that (a) requires reproducing the exact CI harness (tox across the declared envlist) before declaring success, (b) treats every failing test surfaced by the harness as in-scope for a build-fix task, and (c) prompts inspection of test-versus-source timing/precision mismatches and interpreter-availability constraints in tox envlist.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a skill that frames 'fix-build' tasks as: reproduce the CI command exactly, enumerate all failing signals (collection errors, interpreter selection, per-test failures), classify each as configuration vs. code, and only stop when the CI command exits zero. Include heuristics for narrowing the tox envlist to available interpreters and for handling sub-second timestamp precision issues in helper utilities.
diagnoses.target_section: Running Tests / Checklist (or a new 'Diagnosing failing builds' section)

diagnoses.label: premature-success heuristic
diagnoses.general_pattern: None of the skills instruct the agent to keep iterating until the authoritative build command passes; the agent is free to label remaining failures 'pre-existing/unrelated' and finish. This yields false-positive completions on build-repair tasks whose success criterion is exit-zero of the CI script.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Agent trajectory: after fixing ImportError, ran pytest, saw test_record_timestamp fail, wrote 'out of scope for this build-failure task' and finished. Verifier ran run_passed.sh (tox) and failed with the same test_record_timestamp assertion across py310/py311/py312 plus missing interpreters for py37/38/39.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Explicit stop condition tying task completion to the exit status of the project's actual build/test entrypoint (e.g., run_passed.sh / tox) rather than the agent's judgment about which failures are relevant.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document a mandatory verification loop: identify the canonical build command, run it end-to-end, and treat any nonzero exit as unresolved—prohibit categorizing surfaced failures as out-of-scope without evidence that they existed and were tolerated in the original green build.

package_assessment.rationale: The failure mode (declaring a build fixed while the CI harness still exits nonzero, and ignoring tox interpreter/env issues plus a timestamp-precision test failure) is directly attributable to the absence of build-repair guidance and of an exit-zero stop condition in the preloaded skills. A skill package targeting fix-build tasks with explicit verification and scoping rules would have redirected the agent to keep investigating.
